summary: This Dockerfile creates a Docker image for a Docusaurus documentation site. It uses a multi-stage build: first it sets up a Node environment, then builds the static site in a production stage, and finally copies just the built files into a lightweight nginx container to serve them. This approach keeps the final image small by discarding build tools after they're no longer needed.

explanations.1: This special comment tells Docker to use a specific Dockerfile syntax version that enables newer features; it's required to be on the first line.
explanations.7: This starts with a Node.js base image running on Alpine Linux (a tiny Linux distribution). The AS base keyword names this stage so it can be reused by later stages.
explanations.10: This environment variable tells yarn and other tools to not colorize their output, making logs cleaner and more readable.
explanations.13: Corepack is Node's tool manager that lets you use yarn without manually installing it—this command enables it.
explanations.19: This creates a new build stage named building_production that inherits from the base stage, so it has Node.js and corepack already set up.
explanations.22: This command scaffolds a new Docusaurus project from scratch and sets file ownership to the node user (instead of root) for better security.
explanations.31: This copies the package.json and yarn.lock files into the container before running yarn install, which speeds up rebuilds when source code changes but dependencies haven't.
explanations.34: The --immutable flag tells yarn to fail if the lock file doesn't match package.json, ensuring everyone gets identical dependency versions.
explanations.37: This copies all the source code files from your local machine into the container at the /opt/docusaurus directory.
explanations.40: This runs the build command that compiles the Docusaurus source into static HTML/CSS/JS files in the build folder.
explanations.46: This starts a completely new stage based on nginx, a web server. Docker discards the previous Node.js stage here, keeping the final image small.
explanations.49: This COPY --from syntax means copy files from a previous stage (the one that built the site) rather than from your local machine, so only the final built files end up in the nginx container.
